extracted.intended_audience: environmental policy stakeholders, regulated entities, attorneys, and public commenters tracking EPA/Clean Air Act rulemakings related to the Clean Power Plan and related actions
extracted.subtask_description: A Federal Register search-results listing of rulemakings, notices, and related documents matching the term "clean power plan." Used to locate EPA actions, proposals, final rules, and supporting materials relevant to Clean Air Act GHG and NAAQS matters for notice-and-comment and legal analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Finding of contribution as predicate for CAA §111 regulation
rubrics_metrics.description: The EPA must make a finding that GHG emissions from fossil fuel-fired power plants "contribute significantly to dangerous air pollution" as a predicate to regulating GHG emissions from those plants under the Clean Air Act (CAA).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From the proposed repeal excerpt: EPA is proposing that the CAA requires it to make such a finding as a predicate to regulation; the agency also proposes alternatively to make a finding that they do not contribute significantly. This is presented as a statutory-threshold requirement that frames whether regulatory standards under section 111 can be applied to fossil fuel-fired power plants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of emission guideline and standards categories
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulatory requirements at issue may include: emission guidelines for existing fossil fuel-fired steam generating units; CCS-based standards for coal-fired steam generating units undertaking a large modification; and CCS-based standards for new base load stationary combustion turbines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These listed categories identify the specific kinds of section 111/EG standards that may be retained, repealed, or otherwise affected in the rulemaking. They serve as the regulatory designations for which EPA's findings and standards would apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Major questions doctrine (agency clear-statement requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: When an agency asserts regulatory power over a question of vast 'economic and political significance,' the major questions doctrine requires Congress to speak clearly in authorizing that power.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This principle (cited in multiple entries and invoked in court decisions such as West Virginia v. EPA) is applied to evaluate whether EPA had statutory authority for broad extensions of regulatory programs (e.g., the Clean Power Plan). It functions as a legal standard for whether agency action is permissible absent explicit congressional delegation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory-terms interpretation for CAA §202(a)(1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Interpretation of statutory terms like 'air pollution,' 'cause,' 'contribute,' and 'reasonably be anticipated to endanger' is central to determining whether CAA section 202(a)(1) authorizes EPA to prescribe motor vehicle GHG emission standards in response to global climate change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The rescission entry describes using text-based statutory interpretation (together with major questions doctrine reasoning) to determine whether prior endangerment findings and motor vehicle standards are supportable under section 202(a)(1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Clean Data Determination (CDD) criteria and effects
rubrics_metrics.description: Under EPA's Clean Data Policy, where a designated nonattainment area demonstrates attainment of a NAAQS based on complete, quality-assured, and certified ambient air monitoring data for the design value period, EPA may issue a Clean Data Determination (CDD) that suspends certain CAA nonattainment planning requirements for as long as the area continues to attain the NAAQS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The suspension typically applies to obligations such as attainment demonstrations, Reasonably Available Control Measures (RACM)/Reasonably Available Control Technology (RACT), emissions limitations and control measures necessary to provide for attainment, Reasonable Further Progress (RFP) plans, contingency measures, and other related planning SIP requirements. A CDD does not constitute redesignation to attainment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contingency plan requirements for redesignation/maintenance
rubrics_metrics.description: A contingency plan must be an enforceable part of a SIP and must ensure contingency provisions are adopted and implemented expeditiously when triggered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The plan should (1) discuss the measures to be adopted, (2) include a schedule and procedure for adoption and implementation, and (3) require that the State will implement all measures contained in the CAA part D nonattainment plan for the area prior to redesignation. EPA relies on these elements when approving redesignation/maintenance plans (e.g., Klamath Falls, San Joaquin Valley).

rubrics_metrics.name: State Implementation Plan (SIP) content expectations and EPA guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: SIPs addressing attainment-related obligations must meet applicable CAA part D and NAAQS-specific requirements and follow EPA guidance (e.g., the General Preamble and subsequent implementation rules).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA references prior guidance documents (e.g., 'State Implementation Plans; General Preamble for the Implementation of Title I of the Clean Air Act Amendments of 1990' and supplements) and specific NAAQS implementation rules when evaluating SIPs and contingency measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Federal plan requirement when state plan absent (CAA §111 / 40 CFR 60.27)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a State does not have an approved State plan under CAA section 111 that implements the Emission Guidelines, EPA must develop, implement, and enforce a Federal plan for designated facilities and pollutants (published in 40 CFR part 62).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A State or local clean air agency may meet its CAA responsibilities by developing a State plan that is approvable; where it does not, EPA's Federal plan authority applies. Delegation memoranda and MOAs may implement delegated authority for Federal plan elements to state/local agencies once conditions are met.

rubrics_metrics.name: Redesignation to attainment statutory criteria (including maintenance plan elements)
rubrics_metrics.description: For redesignation to attainment, States must submit requests meeting the statutory criteria (e.g., under section 107(d)(3)(E)) and include a maintenance plan demonstrating continued attainment (including motor vehicle emissions budgets, updated state rules, and contingency measures).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA will not redesignate an area unless the statutory elements are satisfied; maintenance plans should demonstrate continued attainment over the required period (example: through 2037) and include enforceable measures and budgets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regional Haze plan requirements and source selection
rubrics_metrics.description: Regional haze plans must address applicable CAA and Regional Haze Rule requirements, including identifying sources (e.g., power plants) that have potential visibility impacts and providing appropriate emissions inventories and analyses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State selections of sources and presentation of source-specific emissions data (tons per year, emissions rates, etc.) are part of meeting the Regional Haze Rule's substantive requirements for visibility protection and reasonable progress demonstrations.

rubrics_metrics.name: EPA approval criteria for revisions to section 111(d) plans
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA reviews proposed revisions to State 111(d) plans (State plans) for consistency with Emissions Guidelines and Compliance Times and with the CAA before approving the revisions into the SIP or federal program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Revisions often update emissions guidelines and compliance schedules for source categories (e.g., municipal solid waste landfills); EPA proposes/approves such revisions following notice-and-comment and required statutory review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Benefit-cost analysis expectations (transparency and geographic disaggregation)
rubrics_metrics.description: When presenting benefit-cost analyses for rules (e.g., the 'Benefit-Cost Rule' discussion), benefits and costs should be appropriately disaggregated such that global benefits (e.g., global social cost of carbon) are not misleadingly compared against domestic-only costs without clear presentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commenters criticized using global SCC benefits compared to U.S.-only costs; EPA guidance/analyses should disaggregate benefits and costs by geographic scope to allow meaningful evaluation and to avoid misleading justifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency procedural requirements for public participation (comment deadlines and submission addresses)
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed rules and notices specify comment deadlines (e.g., 'Comments must be received on or before [date]') and provide submission addresses and contact information for public participation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Federal Register entries repeatedly include explicit DATES and ADDRESSES sections (and contact names/email/phone) that establish the procedural window and methods for notice-and-comment participation; adherence to these deadlines and submission instructions is necessary for timely participation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of CDD on nonattainment planning obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: A final Clean Data Determination suspends certain nonattainment planning obligations for the affected area for as long as the area continues to attain the relevant NAAQS, but does not constitute redesignation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA's final CDD action specifically suspends requirements such as an attainment demonstration, RACM/RACT, emissions limitations and control measures necessary for attainment, an RFP plan, and contingency measures — and explicitly clarifies that suspension lasts until the area no longer attains or is redesignated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of site-specific factors to modify compliance schedules and paperwork dates
rubrics_metrics.description: Under certain rulemakings (e.g., Effluent Limitations Guidelines for the steam electric point source category), EPA may create authority to provide alternative applicability dates and paperwork submission dates based on site-specific factors and may allow transfers between compliance alternatives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This provides flexibility in implementation timelines and compliance-path switching where justified by facility-specific circumstances; such provisions are promulgated through rule text and may include deadline extensions.
